learning_outcomes.text: Understanding the application of nanotechnology in medicine.
Familiarization of students with the techniques of characterizing nanosystems.
Consolidation of the basic principles governing drug delivery to the body and diagnostic methods.
Correlating the characteristics of nanosystems with their toxicity.
Gain experience in studying international scientific literature and presenting scientific topics.
Development of interdisciplinary and critical thinking
Search, analysis, and synthesis of data and information, using the necessary technologies
Promoting free, creative, and inductive thinking

syllabus_topics: Introduction to nanoparticles (e.g., liposomes, micelles, polymeric particles, inorganic nanoparticles, etc.). Synthesis and physicochemical characteristics of nanomaterials.

Drug carriers: structure, encapsulation capacity, and encapsulation efficiency. Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution, pharmacodynamics, metabolism, and absorption of nanoparticles. Targeted and controlled drug delivery with smart nanosystems.
Diagnosis and bioimaging: Types of nanoparticles in medical imaging, diagnosis, and imaging of cells and tissues.
Nanotechnology systems for simultaneous diagnosis and treatment (theranostic agents): Diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.
Nanoparticle toxicity: effect of size, composition, structure, surface chemistry, and dosage.
Case studies and examples of nanomedicine.
Transition from research to clinical application.
Regulatory aspects and ethical issues in nanomedicine.
teaching_methods: Study and analysis of bibliography at home
Communication via the department's website and email
Use of the course website and reliable scientific online sources to find bibliography and present topics to students

assessment_methods.method: Final written exam (problem solving and essay questions)
Assignment/presentation on a topic from international literature

assessment_rules: Students are assessed through a final written exam (combining problem solving and essay questions) and an assignment/presentation on a topic from the international literature. An oral exam is possible for students with learning difficulties. Students can review their written exam results and submit questions to the instructor. The specific weighting percentages for each assessment activity are communicated during the first lecture, provided in writing, and posted on the course website.
